# discorddol

Read a Discord server the way you read a dict.

```python
from discorddol import Guilds, as_text

guilds = Guilds()  # servers your bot can see
channels = guilds["Example Guild"]  # Mapping: channel name -> messages
messages = channels["feedback"]  # list of plain dicts
print(as_text(messages))  # readable transcript
```

Or from the command line:

```bash
discorddol guilds
discorddol channels "Example Guild" --names-only
discorddol transcript "Example Guild" feedback
discorddol export-channel "Example Guild" feedback --out-dir ~/Downloads/discord
discorddol export-guild "Example Guild" --out-dir ~/discord/example-guild
```

## Install

```bash
pip install discorddol
```

## Setting up the bot (five minutes, once)

`discorddol` reads Discord through a bot account. You create it; someone with *Manage Server* on the target server invites it.

1. Go to the [Discord developer portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications) and click **New Application**.
2. **Bot** tab → *Reset Token* → copy the token.
3. **Bot** tab → *Privileged Gateway Intents* → enable **Message Content Intent**. Without this, every message body comes back empty. Leave Presence and Server Members off; `discorddol` does not use them.
4. **Bot** tab → turn **off** *Public Bot*, so only you can invite it.
5. **OAuth2 → URL Generator** → scope `bot`, permissions **View Channels** and **Read Message History** (add **Send Messages** if you want `post-message`, and **Manage Threads** if `export-guild` should include private archived threads; Manage Threads also lets the bot archive and delete threads). Adding a permission later means generating a new invite URL and getting it re-authorized, so pick them now.
6. Open the generated URL, or send it to whoever administers the server, and authorize it there.

Then store the token where `discorddol` looks for it — the `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` environment variable, or [config2py](https://github.com/i2mint/config2py)’s config store:

```bash
printf %s "<your token>" > ~/.config/config2py/configs/DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
chmod 600 ~/.config/config2py/configs/DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
```

Sanity check — if this returns an empty list, the bot exists but has not been invited anywhere yet:

```bash
discorddol guilds
```

A bot only sees channels its role grants access to. Private channels need an explicit permission overwrite, which the server’s admin has to add.

## The stores

Everything is a `collections.abc.Mapping`, so the usual idioms work: `in`, `len`, `.keys()`, `.items()`, dict comprehensions.

| Store                     | Keys                           | Values                             |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `Guilds()`                | guild name (id if ambiguous)   | a `Channels` store                 |
| `Channels(guild_id)`      | channel name (id if ambiguous) | list of message dicts              |
| `Channels(guild_id).info` | same keys                      | channel metadata dict              |
| `ChannelLogs(folder)`     | channel id                     | messages written by `export-guild` |
| `CachedAttachments()`     | channel id                     | locally cached attachment records  |

Channel lookup accepts a name, a `#name`, or an id, so all three of these are the same channel:

```python
channels["feedback"]
channels["#feedback"]
channels["123456789012345678"]
```

Threads are where a lot of real discussion ends up. They are not merged in by default, because it changes what “the channel” means:

```python
# messages and thread replies, in time order
Channels(guild_id, include_threads=True)["feedback"]
```

A forum has no messages of its own, only posts, which are threads; so a forum maps to an empty list, and with `include_threads=True` to the messages of its posts.

Fetching a busy channel is slow and rate-limited, so pass any `MutableMapping` as a cache and repeat reads come from it. A `dict` works; so does anything from [dol](https://github.com/i2mint/dol), which is how you get a persistent one:

```python
from dol import JsonFiles

channels = Channels(guild_id, cache_store=JsonFiles("~/.cache/discord"))
```

Use `JsonFiles` rather than `Files` — cached values are lists of dicts, not bytes. The cache is keyed by channel id and survives across processes, so a second run of a long export starts from what the first one already fetched.

## Exporting a whole server

`export-guild` writes every channel the bot can read to disk, one JSONL file per channel, and is safe to run again:

```bash
discorddol export-guild "Example Guild" --out-dir ~/discord/example-guild
```

```default
~/discord/example-guild/
    manifest.json                what was exported, what was skipped, and why
    messages/<channel_id>.jsonl  one message per line, oldest first
```

- **Exported:** text and announcement channels, forum posts, and threads: active ones, archived ones, and private archived ones when the bot has *Manage Threads*. Without that permission, the manifest lists the private archived threads it could not fetch under `not_fetched`, and the export carries on.
- **Skipped:** categories, voice and stage channels, and any channel whose history Discord will not let the bot read. Each is listed under `skipped` with its reason.
- **Running it again** fetches only messages newer than the last line of each file, and does not fetch a channel whose latest message is already there. An interrupted export picks up where it stopped. Only one export at a time can write to a folder.
- **Content check:** before writing anything, it samples recent messages written by people, a few from each channel, and refuses to go on if most of them are blank, which is what a missing *Message Content Intent* looks like. A few blank messages, such as stickers or polls, do not stop it. If that first sample is small, the export keeps judging what it fetches and stops as soon as the messages turn out blank. An export made without the intent stays blank, because running it again does not refetch messages it already has: delete it and export again. If the messages really are blank, pass `--skip-preflight`.

Each entry under `channels` in the manifest gives the channel’s id, name, kind (`text`, `announcement`, `forum` or `thread`), parent, file, message count, the dates of its first and last messages, the channel record as Discord described it, and a `status`: `exported`; `skipped`, when Discord refused its history this time (its file keeps what earlier runs got); or `not in last run`, for a channel deleted or hidden from the bot since an earlier run. Every page of history and every thread listing is its own API call, so a large server takes a while; progress goes to stderr unless you pass `--quiet`.

Without `--out-dir`, the export goes to `exports/<guild id>` in discorddol’s data folder: `$DISCORDDOL_DATA_DIR` if that is set, else `~/.local/share/discorddol`.

The same from Python, where the guild is given by id, and reading an export back:

```python
from discorddol import ChannelLogs, export_guild

manifest = export_guild("123456789012345678", "~/discord/example-guild")
messages = ChannelLogs("~/discord/example-guild/messages")
messages["234567890123456789"]  # one channel's messages, oldest first
```

## Recovering a deleted channel

**Discord has no undelete.** Deleting a channel destroys its messages server-side. No bot, no API call, and no amount of owner permission brings them back, so this package cannot recover the text of a deleted channel and neither can anything else.

What *is* recoverable is attachments, because the desktop client is an Electron app and every image it displayed passed through Chromium’s on-disk cache. Those URLs embed the channel id, so:

```bash
discorddol find-deleted-channels "Example Guild"   # cached channel ids the server no longer lists
discorddol recover-attachments <channel_id> --out-dir ~/Downloads/recovered
```

`find-deleted-channels` returns *candidates*, not a verdict: an id shows up as an orphan if this machine cached attachments from it and the server does not currently list it, which also covers other servers and channels the bot cannot see. Confirm before concluding.

This matters because Discord attachment URLs are signed and expire — knowing the URL is not enough to re-download it. The cache holds the payload itself. `recover-attachments` needs no token and no network.

For message **text** from a deleted channel, the only route is a [Discord data export](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/360004027692) (Settings → Data & Privacy → *Request all of my Data*). It contains your own sent messages filed by channel id, including channels that no longer exist — which is exactly what the channel id from `find-deleted-channels` is for. It covers only your own messages, so each participant has to request their own.

The cache reader is read-only and never writes to, moves, or deletes anything in the live cache directory that the running Discord client owns.

## Swapping the pieces

Four seams, each one keyword argument:

| Seam              | Default                       | Swap it for                                              |
|-------------------|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `token`           | env var, then config2py store | any string you resolve yourself                          |
| `backend`         | `DiscordRest` (live API)      | `DictBackend` for tests and fixtures, or your own reader |
| `message_to_dict` | full JSON-safe record         | a slimmer schema for LLM context                         |
| `cache_store`     | `None` (always fetch)         | any `MutableMapping`, e.g. a `dol` store                 |

`export_guild` takes the same `token` and `backend`.

`DictBackend` is a real backend, not a mock, which is what makes the test suite runnable without credentials:

```python
from discorddol import Channels, DictBackend

backend = DictBackend(
    channels={"1": [{"id": "10", "name": "dev"}]},
    messages={"10": [{"id": "100", "clean_content": "hi"}]},
)
Channels("1", backend=backend)["dev"]
```

## Other surfaces

`discorddol.tools` is the single list of verbs, written as plain functions taking and returning JSON-able values, knowing nothing about MCP, HTTP or argparse. The CLI dispatches over that list, and an MCP server needs no change to the core:

```python
from py2mcp import mk_mcp_from_refs

mk_mcp_from_refs(["discorddol.tools:transcript", "discorddol.tools:channels"])
```

# _autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md

# discorddol.base

Core of discorddol: a Discord read backend and the `Mapping` stores over it.

The design has one hinge: **the backend**. Everything user-facing is a `Mapping`
whose data comes from a backend object exposing five methods – `guilds`,
`channels`, `threads`, `archived_threads`, `messages` – each returning plain
JSON-able dicts. The default backend ([`DiscordRest`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.DiscordRest)) talks to the live Discord
API; swapping it for one that reads a Discord data export, or a dict of fixtures,
changes nothing above it.

The stores:

```default
Guilds()                       # Mapping: guild name/id -> Channels
Channels(guild_id)             # Mapping: channel name/id -> list of message dicts
Channels(guild_id).info        # Mapping: channel name/id -> channel metadata
```

so the common case reads like plain Python:

```default
from discorddol import Guilds

msgs = Guilds()['Example Guild']['feedback']
```

`DiscordRest` uses discord.py in REST-only mode – it logs in over HTTP but never
opens a gateway connection. That makes every call a one-shot fetch that returns
promptly, instead of a bot process you have to keep alive and shut down.

### Module Attributes

| [`CHANNEL_KINDS`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.CHANNEL_KINDS)   | Discord's channel type (`str(channel.type)`) -> the kind discorddol reports.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`get_token`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.get_token)([key])                         | Resolve a Discord token: environment variable first, then the config2py store.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`message_to_dict`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.message_to_dict)(message)                 | Serialize a `discord.Message` to a plain, JSON-safe dict.                        |
| [`channel_to_dict`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.channel_to_dict)(channel)                 | Serialize a channel or thread to a plain dict.                                   |
| [`channel_kind`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.channel_kind)(record)                     | The kind of a channel record: `'text'`, `'announcement'`, `'forum'`, ...         |
| [`as_text`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.as_text)(messages, \*[, with_timestamps]) | Render message dicts as a readable transcript -- the form you feed to an LLM.    |

### Classes

| [`DiscordRest`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.DiscordRest)(\*[, token, message_to_dict])          | Live Discord backend: discord.py in REST-only mode (login, no gateway).                                   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DictBackend`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.DictBackend)(\*[, guilds, channels, messages, ...]) | In-memory backend over plain dicts.                                                                       |
| [`Channels`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.Channels)(guild_id, \*[, backend, token, ...])      | Mapping of one guild's channels: key -> list of message dicts.                                            |
| [`Guilds`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.Guilds)(\*[, backend, token, cache_store])          | Mapping of the servers the bot can see: key -> [`Channels`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.Channels). |

### discorddol.base.CHANNEL_KINDS *= {'category': 'category', 'forum': 'forum', 'media': 'media', 'news': 'announcement', 'news_thread': 'thread', 'private_thread': 'thread', 'public_thread': 'thread', 'stage_voice': 'stage', 'text': 'text', 'voice': 'voice'}*

Discord’s channel type (`str(channel.type)`) -> the kind discorddol reports.

### *class* discorddol.base.Channels(guild_id, , backend=None, token=None, cache_store=None, include_threads=False, \*\*message_kwargs)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

Mapping of one guild’s channels: key -> list of message dicts.

Keys are channel names when unambiguous, and channel ids otherwise. Lookup accepts
either form, plus a leading `#`, so `channels['#dev']` and `channels['dev']`
and `channels['10']` all work.

A forum or a category has no messages of its own, so it maps to an empty list; with
`include_threads=True` a forum maps to the messages of its posts.

```pycon
>>> backend = DictBackend(
...     channels={'1': [{'id': '10', 'name': 'dev'}, {'id': '11', 'name': 'feedback'}]},
...     messages={'10': [{'id': '100', 'content': 'hi'}]},
... )
>>> channels = Channels('1', backend=backend)
>>> sorted(channels)
['dev', 'feedback']
>>> channels['dev']
[{'id': '100', 'content': 'hi'}]
>>> channels.info['dev']['id']
'10'
```

#### refresh()

Drop the cached channel listing so the next access refetches it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Channels`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.Channels)

### *class* discorddol.base.DictBackend(, guilds=None, channels=None, messages=None, threads=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

In-memory backend over plain dicts. Real enough for tests, fixtures and exports.

```pycon
>>> backend = DictBackend(
...     guilds=[{'id': '1', 'name': 'Example Guild'}],
...     channels={'1': [{'id': '10', 'name': 'dev'}]},
...     messages={'10': [{'id': '100', 'content': 'hi'}]},
... )
>>> backend.guilds()
[{'id': '1', 'name': 'Example Guild'}]
>>> backend.messages('10')
[{'id': '100', 'content': 'hi'}]
```

#### archived_threads(channel_id, , private=False)

The threads under `channel_id` marked `archived`: public, or private ones.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

```pycon
>>> backend = DictBackend(threads={'10': [
...     {'id': '20', 'type': 'public_thread', 'archived': True},
...     {'id': '21', 'type': 'private_thread', 'archived': True},
...     {'id': '22', 'type': 'public_thread'},
... ]})
>>> [t['id'] for t in backend.archived_threads('10')]
['20']
>>> [t['id'] for t in backend.archived_threads('10', private=True)]
['21']
```

#### messages(channel_id, , limit=None, after=None, before=None, oldest_first=True, \*\*kwargs)

Stored messages, filtered the way [`DiscordRest.messages()`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.DiscordRest.messages) filters them.

Messages are stored oldest first. `after` and `before` take a message id,
compared as a Discord snowflake (an integer), or a datetime, compared with each
message’s `created_at`. Other keyword arguments are accepted and ignored.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

```pycon
>>> backend = DictBackend(messages={'10': [{'id': '1'}, {'id': '2'}, {'id': '3'}]})
>>> [m['id'] for m in backend.messages('10', after='1', limit=1)]
['2']
>>> [m['id'] for m in backend.messages('10', oldest_first=False, limit=1)]
['3']
```

### *class* discorddol.base.DiscordRest(\*, token=None, message_to_dict=<function message_to_dict>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Live Discord backend: discord.py in REST-only mode (login, no gateway).

```pycon
>>> backend = DiscordRest(token='fake')  # no network happens until a call is made
>>> backend.token
'fake'
```

#### archived_threads(channel_id, , private=False)

List a channel’s archived threads: the public ones, or the private ones.

Listing private archived threads needs the Manage Threads permission; without it
Discord answers 403, raised as [`Forbidden`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.Forbidden). Only text channels hold
private threads, so `private=True` on any other channel returns an empty list.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### channels(guild_id)

List a guild’s channels, including its currently active threads.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### guilds()

List servers the bot has been added to.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### messages(channel_id, , limit=None, after=None, before=None, oldest_first=True)

Fetch a channel’s message history. `limit=None` means the whole thing.

`after` and `before` take a datetime or a message id, so the id of the last
message already stored works as a cursor.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### send_message(channel_id, text)

Post a message to a channel. The one write operation; needs Send Messages.

Read access is what discorddol is for – this exists so that acting on what you
read does not require a second library.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### threads(channel_id)

List a channel’s threads, archived ones included – often where the content is.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

The token, resolved lazily so constructing a backend never needs credentials.

Bases: [`PermissionError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#PermissionError)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

Mapping of the servers the bot can see: key -> [`Channels`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.Channels).

Keys are guild names when unambiguous, ids otherwise; lookup accepts either.

```pycon
>>> backend = DictBackend(
...     guilds=[{'id': '1', 'name': 'Example Guild'}],
...     channels={'1': [{'id': '10', 'name': 'dev'}]},
```

### discorddol.base.as_text(messages, , with_timestamps=True)

Render message dicts as a readable transcript – the form you feed to an LLM.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> print(as_text([{'created_at': '2026-09-04T10:00:00',
...                 'author': {'display_name': 'ada'},
...                 'clean_content': 'hello'}]))
[2026-09-04T10:00] ada: hello
```

### discorddol.base.channel_kind(record)

The kind of a channel record: `'text'`, `'announcement'`, `'forum'`, …

A record without a type counts as a text channel, which is what a hand-written
fixture usually means. An unknown type comes back as it is.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> channel_kind({'type': 'news'})
'announcement'
>>> channel_kind({'type': 'ChannelType.stage_voice'})
'stage'
>>> channel_kind({'id': '10'})
'text'
```

### discorddol.base.channel_to_dict(channel)

Serialize a channel or thread to a plain dict.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### discorddol.base.get_token(key='DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN')

Resolve a Discord token: environment variable first, then the config2py store.

Raises a [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) naming the exact fix rather than a bare `KeyError`,
because a missing token is the single most common first-run failure.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### discorddol.base.message_to_dict(message)

Serialize a `discord.Message` to a plain, JSON-safe dict.

A message that is only a sticker, a poll or a forward has no text, attachments or
embeds of its own, so those live under `stickers`, `poll` (`None` when the
message has none) and `forwarded` (one entry per forwarded message, which is how
Discord holds a forward: a snapshot of the original).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/discorddol.export.html.md

# discorddol.export

Export a whole guild to disk: every channel the bot can read, one JSONL file each.

[`export_guild()`](_autosummary/discorddol.export.html.md#discorddol.export.export_guild) walks a guild’s channel listing and writes:

```default
<out_dir>/
    manifest.json                 what was exported, what was skipped, and why
    messages/<channel_id>.jsonl   one message dict per line, oldest first
```

What gets exported, by channel kind (see [`discorddol.base.CHANNEL_KINDS`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.CHANNEL_KINDS)):

- **text** and **announcement** channels: their own history, then their threads;
- **forum** and **media** channels: their posts, which are threads;
- **threads**: the active ones, the public archived ones, and the private archived ones
  when the bot has Manage Threads. When it does not, the manifest lists what was not
  fetched under `not_fetched`, and the export carries on.

Categories, voice and stage channels are not exported, and neither is a channel whose
history Discord refuses to hand over. Each is listed under `skipped` with its reason.

**Incremental and resumable.** A channel’s file is its own cursor: a run reads the id on
the file’s last complete line and fetches only messages after it, a page at a time,
appending as it goes. An interrupted run loses at most the page it was writing; the next
run drops a half-written last line before appending, and carries on from there. A
channel whose `last_message_id` is already in its file is not fetched at all. Only one
run at a time may write to a folder; another is refused with [`ExportInProgress`](_autosummary/discorddol.export.html.md#discorddol.export.ExportInProgress).

**Content check.** Without the Message Content intent, Discord still returns every
message, but with its text, attachments and embeds blanked. An export in that state
looks like a success and holds nothing. So before anything is written,
[`check_message_content()`](_autosummary/discorddol.export.html.md#discorddol.export.check_message_content) samples recent messages written by people, a few from
each channel, and refuses to go on when most of them are blank. Until a full sample has
been judged, the export goes on judging the messages it fetches in the same way, and
refuses as soon as they show blank bodies, or at the latest when the run ends. Messages
written before that point stay on disk, so delete an export refused this way.

### Functions

|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* discorddol.export.ChannelLogs(rootdir)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

Mapping: channel id -> that channel’s exported messages, one JSONL file each.

The export’s writer as well as its reader: [`extend()`](_autosummary/discorddol.export.html.md#discorddol.export.ChannelLogs.extend) appends messages, and
[`summary()`](_autosummary/discorddol.export.html.md#discorddol.export.ChannelLogs.summary) gives a file’s message count, date range and cursor, parsing only
its first and last lines. Files hold messages oldest first, in the order appended.
Reading never changes a file; a half-written last line is ignored until the next
[`extend()`](_autosummary/discorddol.export.html.md#discorddol.export.ChannelLogs.extend) drops it.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
...     logs = ChannelLogs(tmp)
...     _ = logs.extend('10', [{'id': '1', 'created_at': '2026-01-01T09:00:00'}])
...     _ = logs.extend('10', [{'id': '2', 'created_at': '2026-01-02T09:00:00'}])
...     print(list(logs), [m['id'] for m in logs['10']], logs.summary('10'))
['10'] ['1', '2'] {'message_count': 2, 'first_message_at': '2026-01-01T09:00:00', 'last_message_at': '2026-01-02T09:00:00', 'last_message_id': '2'}
```

#### extend(channel_id, messages)

Append messages to a channel’s file, creating it if needed. Returns how many.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

#### path(channel_id)

The JSONL file of one channel.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

#### summary(channel_id)

A channel’s message count, first and last dates, and last id (its cursor).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### *exception* discorddol.export.ExportInProgress

Bases: [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError)

Another export is already writing to the same folder.

### *exception* discorddol.export.MessageContentMissing

Bases: [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError)

Message bodies come back blank: the bot’s Message Content Intent is off.

### discorddol.export.check_message_content(backend, channels, , sample_size=20, min_channels=4, max_blank_share=0.5)

Refuse to export blank messages: sample recent messages and check their content.

Fetches the newest messages of each channel in `channels` (records with an
`id`), one call per channel, until `sample_size` messages written by people have
been collected. No channel supplies more than `sample_size // min_channels` of
them, so one channel full of stickers cannot decide the verdict. System notices and
bot messages do not count: a notice can be blank anyway, and a bot’s own messages
keep their content without the intent. A message is blank when it has no text, no
attachments and no embeds, which is how Discord sends every message when the intent
is off.

Raises [`MessageContentMissing`](_autosummary/discorddol.export.html.md#discorddol.export.MessageContentMissing), naming the fix, when more than
`max_blank_share` of the sample is blank. Returns `{'status': 'passed',
'checked', 'blank'}`, or `{'status': 'inconclusive', 'checked': 0, 'blank': 0}`
when there was nothing to judge.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

```pycon
>>> from discorddol.base import DictBackend
>>> backend = DictBackend(messages={'10': [{'id': '1', 'content': 'hi'}]})
>>> check_message_content(backend, [{'id': '10'}])
{'status': 'passed', 'checked': 1, 'blank': 0}
```

### discorddol.export.default_export_dir(guild_id)

Where a guild’s export goes when no `out_dir` is given: `<data>/exports/<id>`.

`<data>` is `$DISCORDDOL_DATA_DIR` when that is set, else discorddol’s app data
folder (`~/.local/share/discorddol` on macOS and Linux). Never inside a
repository, so exported messages are not committed by accident.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### discorddol.export.export_guild(guild_id, out_dir, , backend=None, token=None, guild_name=None, page_size=1000, private_threads=True, preflight=True, sample_size=20, log=None)

Export every channel of a guild the bot can read into `out_dir`.

Returns the manifest, which is also written to `out_dir`. Re-running on the same
`out_dir` fetches only what is new (see the module docstring).
`private_threads=False` does not ask for private archived threads.
`preflight=False` turns the content check off; `sample_size` is how many
messages make a full sample for it. `log` gets one line per channel.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> from discorddol.base import DictBackend
>>> backend = DictBackend(
...     channels={'1': [
...         {'id': '10', 'name': 'general', 'type': 'text'},
...         {'id': '11', 'name': 'Community', 'type': 'category'},
...     ]},
...     messages={'10': [{'id': '100', 'content': 'hi', 'created_at': '2026-01-01'}]},
... )
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
...     manifest = export_guild('1', tmp, backend=backend)
>>> [(c['name'], c['kind'], c['message_count']) for c in manifest['channels']]
[('general', 'text', 1)]
>>> [(s['name'], s['reason']) for s in manifest['skipped']]
[('Community', 'category: it groups other channels and holds no messages')]
```


# _autosummary/discorddol.html.md

# discorddol

Discord data object layers: read guilds, channels, threads and messages as Mappings.

Read a Discord server the way you read a dict:

```default
from discorddol import Guilds

guilds = Guilds()                       # servers the bot can see
channels = guilds['Example Guild']      # Mapping: channel name -> messages
messages = channels['feedback']         # list of message dicts
print(as_text(messages))                # readable transcript
```

Credentials come from the `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` environment variable, falling back to
`config2py`’s store (`~/.config/config2py/configs/DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`). See the README
for the five-minute bot setup, including the Message Content Intent that message bodies
depend on.

To export a whole server to disk – every readable channel, resumably – see
[`discorddol.export`](_autosummary/discorddol.export.html.md#module-discorddol.export).

For a channel that has been **deleted**, see [`discorddol.local_cache`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#module-discorddol.local_cache): Discord has
no undelete, but the desktop client’s on-disk cache still holds attachments it displayed.

### Functions

| [`as_text`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.as_text)(messages, \*[, with_timestamps])         | Render message dicts as a readable transcript -- the form you feed to an LLM.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`get_token`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.get_token)([key])                                 | Resolve a Discord token: environment variable first, then the config2py store.  |
| [`message_to_dict`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.message_to_dict)(message)                         | Serialize a `discord.Message` to a plain, JSON-safe dict.                       |
| [`channel_to_dict`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.channel_to_dict)(channel)                         | Serialize a channel or thread to a plain dict.                                  |
| [`channel_kind`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.channel_kind)(record)                             | The kind of a channel record: `'text'`, `'announcement'`, `'forum'`, ...        |
| [`export_guild`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.export_guild)(guild_id, out_dir, \*[, ...])       | Export every channel of a guild the bot can read into `out_dir`.                |
| [`cached_channel_ids`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.cached_channel_ids)(\*[, cache_dir])              | Channel ids appearing in cached attachment URLs, counted by cached attachment.  |
| [`orphan_channel_ids`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.orphan_channel_ids)(guild_id, \*[, backend, ...]) | Cached channel ids that no longer exist in `guild_id` -- deleted channels.      |
| [`extract_channel_attachments`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.extract_channel_attachments)(channel_id, \*, ...) | Write every cached attachment belonging to `channel_id` out to `out_dir`.       |

### Classes

| [`Guilds`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.Guilds)(\*[, backend, token, cache_store])          | Mapping of the servers the bot can see: key -> [`Channels`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.Channels).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* discorddol.Channels(guild_id, , backend=None, token=None, cache_store=None, include_threads=False, \*\*message_kwargs)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

Mapping of one guild’s channels: key -> list of message dicts.

Keys are channel names when unambiguous, and channel ids otherwise. Lookup accepts
either form, plus a leading `#`, so `channels['#dev']` and `channels['dev']`
and `channels['10']` all work.

A forum or a category has no messages of its own, so it maps to an empty list; with
`include_threads=True` a forum maps to the messages of its posts.

```pycon
>>> backend = DictBackend(
...     channels={'1': [{'id': '10', 'name': 'dev'}, {'id': '11', 'name': 'feedback'}]},
...     messages={'10': [{'id': '100', 'content': 'hi'}]},
... )
>>> channels = Channels('1', backend=backend)
>>> sorted(channels)
['dev', 'feedback']
>>> channels['dev']
[{'id': '100', 'content': 'hi'}]
>>> channels.info['dev']['id']
'10'
```

#### refresh()

Drop the cached channel listing so the next access refetches it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Channels`](_autosummary/discorddol.base.html.md#discorddol.base.Channels)

### *class* discorddol.DictBackend(, guilds=None, channels=None, messages=None, threads=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

In-memory backend over plain dicts. Real enough for tests, fixtures and exports.

```pycon
>>> backend = DictBackend(
...     guilds=[{'id': '1', 'name': 'Example Guild'}],
...     channels={'1': [{'id': '10', 'name': 'dev'}]},
...     messages={'10': [{'id': '100', 'content': 'hi'}]},
... )
>>> backend.guilds()
[{'id': '1', 'name': 'Example Guild'}]
>>> backend.messages('10')
[{'id': '100', 'content': 'hi'}]
```

#### archived_threads(channel_id, , private=False)

The threads under `channel_id` marked `archived`: public, or private ones.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

```pycon
>>> backend = DictBackend(threads={'10': [
...     {'id': '20', 'type': 'public_thread', 'archived': True},
...     {'id': '21', 'type': 'private_thread', 'archived': True},
...     {'id': '22', 'type': 'public_thread'},
... ]})
>>> [t['id'] for t in backend.archived_threads('10')]
['20']
>>> [t['id'] for t in backend.archived_threads('10', private=True)]
['21']
```

#### messages(channel_id, , limit=None, after=None, before=None, oldest_first=True, \*\*kwargs)

Stored messages, filtered the way [`DiscordRest.messages()`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.DiscordRest.messages) filters them.

Messages are stored oldest first. `after` and `before` take a message id,
compared as a Discord snowflake (an integer), or a datetime, compared with each
message’s `created_at`. Other keyword arguments are accepted and ignored.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

```pycon
>>> backend = DictBackend(messages={'10': [{'id': '1'}, {'id': '2'}, {'id': '3'}]})
>>> [m['id'] for m in backend.messages('10', after='1', limit=1)]
['2']
>>> [m['id'] for m in backend.messages('10', oldest_first=False, limit=1)]
['3']
```

#### archived_threads(channel_id, , private=False)

List a channel’s archived threads: the public ones, or the private ones.

Listing private archived threads needs the Manage Threads permission; without it
Discord answers 403, raised as [`Forbidden`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.Forbidden). Only text channels hold
private threads, so `private=True` on any other channel returns an empty list.

* **Return type:**

Write every cached attachment belonging to `channel_id` out to `out_dir`.

Returns one record per file written, with the original filename and the bytes
recovered. Extraction is heuristic – it locates a known file signature inside the
cache entry and reads to the entry’s EOF record – so verify anything that matters
by opening it.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### discorddol.get_token(key='DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN')

Resolve a Discord token: environment variable first, then the config2py store.

Raises a [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) naming the exact fix rather than a bare `KeyError`,
because a missing token is the single most common first-run failure.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### discorddol.message_to_dict(message)

Serialize a `discord.Message` to a plain, JSON-safe dict.

A message that is only a sticker, a poll or a forward has no text, attachments or
embeds of its own, so those live under `stickers`, `poll` (`None` when the
message has none) and `forwarded` (one entry per forwarded message, which is how
Discord holds a forward: a snapshot of the original).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### discorddol.orphan_channel_ids(guild_id, , backend=None, token=None, cache_dir=None)

Cached channel ids that no longer exist in `guild_id` – deleted channels.

Returns `{'orphans': {channel_id: count}, 'live': {channel_id: count}}`, each
ordered by count descending.

An id under `orphans` is a *candidate*, not a verdict: it is a channel this
machine cached attachments from that is not currently visible in `guild_id`. That
covers deleted channels, but also channels in other servers and channels the bot
lacks permission to see. Cross-check a candidate against
[`extract_channel_attachments()`](_autosummary/discorddol.html.md#discorddol.extract_channel_attachments) output before concluding anything.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> from discorddol.base import DictBackend
>>> backend = DictBackend(channels={'1': [{'id': '10', 'name': 'dev'}]})
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
...     result = orphan_channel_ids('1', backend=backend, cache_dir=tmp)
>>> sorted(result)
['live', 'orphans']
```

# _autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md

# discorddol.local_cache

Read the Discord desktop client’s on-disk HTTP cache – including for deleted channels.

Discord has no undelete: deleting a channel destroys its messages server-side, and no
API, bot or owner permission brings them back. But the desktop client is an Electron
app, so every attachment it ever displayed passed through Chromium’s HTTP cache and the
**bytes are still on disk**. Attachment URLs embed the channel id:

```default
https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/{channel_id}/{attachment_id}/{filename}
```

which gives a recovery path for a channel that no longer exists:

1. [`cached_channel_ids()`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#discorddol.local_cache.cached_channel_ids) – every channel id with cached attachments.
2. [`orphan_channel_ids()`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#discorddol.local_cache.orphan_channel_ids) – those that no longer resolve against the live API.
   A deleted channel shows up here.
3. [`extract_channel_attachments()`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#discorddol.local_cache.extract_channel_attachments) – write those bytes back out to real files.

Step 3 matters because Discord attachment URLs are signed and expire, so re-downloading
them is not an option even when you know the URL. The cache holds the payload itself.

Message **text** is not recoverable this way – Discord’s API responses are sent
`no-store` and never hit the disk cache. For text, request your Discord data export
(Settings -> Data & Privacy -> Request all of my Data), which files your own sent
messages by channel id, including channels that no longer exist. The channel id from
step 2 is what lets you find the right folder in that export.

This is a read-only reader. It never writes to, moves, or deletes anything in the live
cache directory, which the running Discord client owns.

### Functions

| [`discord_cache_dir`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#discorddol.local_cache.discord_cache_dir)(\*[, app])                     | Default Discord desktop cache directory for this platform.                     |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`cached_attachment_refs`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#discorddol.local_cache.cached_attachment_refs)(\*[, cache_dir])          | Yield one record per cached attachment URL found in the cache.                 |
| [`cached_channel_ids`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#discorddol.local_cache.cached_channel_ids)(\*[, cache_dir])              | Channel ids appearing in cached attachment URLs, counted by cached attachment. |
| [`orphan_channel_ids`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#discorddol.local_cache.orphan_channel_ids)(guild_id, \*[, backend, ...]) | Cached channel ids that no longer exist in `guild_id` -- deleted channels.     |
| [`extract_channel_attachments`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#discorddol.local_cache.extract_channel_attachments)(channel_id, \*, ...) | Write every cached attachment belonging to `channel_id` out to `out_dir`.      |

### Classes

| [`CachedAttachments`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#discorddol.local_cache.CachedAttachments)(\*[, cache_dir])   | Mapping: channel id -> list of cached attachment records on this machine.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* discorddol.local_cache.CachedAttachments(, cache_dir=None)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

Mapping: channel id -> list of cached attachment records on this machine.

A read-only view of what the local Discord client still holds, usable after the
channel itself is gone.

### discorddol.local_cache.cached_attachment_refs(, cache_dir=None)

Yield one record per cached attachment URL found in the cache.

Each record has `channel_id`, `attachment_id`, `filename` and `cache_file`.
Streams rather than accumulating, so a multi-gigabyte cache stays cheap to scan.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### discorddol.local_cache.cached_channel_ids(, cache_dir=None)

Channel ids appearing in cached attachment URLs, counted by cached attachment.

The counts are a usefully blunt signal: a channel with many cached attachments was
one you actually spent time in.

* **Return type:**
  [`Counter`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.html#collections.Counter)

### discorddol.local_cache.discord_cache_dir(, app='discord')

Default Discord desktop cache directory for this platform.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

```pycon
>>> isinstance(discord_cache_dir(), Path)
True
```

by opening it.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### discorddol.local_cache.orphan_channel_ids(guild_id, , backend=None, token=None, cache_dir=None)

Cached channel ids that no longer exist in `guild_id` – deleted channels.

Returns `{'orphans': {channel_id: count}, 'live': {channel_id: count}}`, each
ordered by count descending.

An id under `orphans` is a *candidate*, not a verdict: it is a channel this
machine cached attachments from that is not currently visible in `guild_id`. That
covers deleted channels, but also channels in other servers and channels the bot
lacks permission to see. Cross-check a candidate against
[`extract_channel_attachments()`](_autosummary/discorddol.local_cache.html.md#discorddol.local_cache.extract_channel_attachments) output before concluding anything.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

```pycon

>>> from discorddol.base import DictBackend
>>> backend = DictBackend(channels={'1': [{'id': '10', 'name': 'dev'}]})
```

# _autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md

# discorddol.tools

SSOT verb list for discorddol: plain functions, JSON-able in, JSON-able out.

Deliberately agnostic about how it is reached. This module knows nothing about MCP,
HTTP, argparse or any agent host; a wrapper references e.g. `discorddol.tools:messages`
and gets a clean JSON-ready value back. `__main__.py` builds the CLI off the same list
(`DISPATCH_FUNCS`), so a new verb becomes available on every surface at once.

### Module Attributes

| [`DISPATCH_FUNCS`](_autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md#discorddol.tools.DISPATCH_FUNCS)   | The SSOT list every surface dispatches over.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`guilds`](_autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md#discorddol.tools.guilds)(\*[, token])                                | List the Discord servers the bot has been added to.                            |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`channels`](_autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md#discorddol.tools.channels)(guild, \*[, token, names_only])           | List a server's channels and threads.                                          |
| [`messages`](_autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md#discorddol.tools.messages)(guild, channel, \*[, token, limit, ...])  | Fetch a channel's messages as dicts.                                           |
| [`transcript`](_autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md#discorddol.tools.transcript)(guild, channel, \*[, token, ...])       | Render a channel as readable transcript text -- the form to feed an LLM.       |
| [`export_channel`](_autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md#discorddol.tools.export_channel)(guild, channel, \*[, out_dir, ...]) | Export a channel (threads included by default) to a JSON file.                 |
| [`export_guild`](_autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md#discorddol.tools.export_guild)(guild, \*[, out_dir, token, ...])     | Export every channel the bot can read in a server, one JSONL file per channel. |
| [`find_deleted_channels`](_autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md#discorddol.tools.find_deleted_channels)(guild, \*[, token, ...])     | Find channel ids cached on this machine that no longer exist in a server.      |
| [`recover_attachments`](_autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md#discorddol.tools.recover_attachments)(channel_id, \*[, ...])         | Write out every attachment this machine cached for a channel, deleted or not.  |
| [`post_message`](_autosummary/discorddol.tools.html.md#discorddol.tools.post_message)(channel_id, text, \*[, token])        | Post a message to a channel.                                                   |

### discorddol.tools.DISPATCH_FUNCS *= [<function guilds>, <function channels>, <function messages>, <function transcript>, <function export_channel>, <function export_guild>, <function find_deleted_channels>, <function recover_attachments>, <function post_message>]*

The SSOT list every surface dispatches over. Add a verb here, get it everywhere.

### discorddol.tools.channels(guild, , token=None, names_only=False)

List a server’s channels and threads. `guild` may be a guild name or id.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)] | [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### discorddol.tools.export_channel(guild, channel, , out_dir='~/Downloads/discord', token=None, include_threads=True)

Export a channel (threads included by default) to a JSON file. Returns a summary.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### discorddol.tools.export_guild(guild, , out_dir=None, token=None, skip_preflight=False, quiet=False)

Export every channel the bot can read in a server, one JSONL file per channel.

Text and announcement channels, forum posts, and threads (active, archived, and
private archived ones when the bot has Manage Threads) are exported. Categories,
voice and stage channels are skipped, and the manifest says why. Re-running on the
same `out_dir` fetches only new messages, so an interrupted export resumes.

Before writing anything, recent messages are sampled to check that message bodies
are not blank, which is what a disabled Message Content Intent looks like;
`skip_preflight` turns that check off. Only one export at a time may write to a
folder. `out_dir` defaults to
`exports/<guild id>` in discorddol’s data folder. Progress goes to stderr unless
`quiet`. Returns a summary; the details are in the manifest.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### discorddol.tools.find_deleted_channels(guild, , token=None, cache_dir=None)

Find channel ids cached on this machine that no longer exist in a server.

Discord cannot undelete a channel, but the desktop client cached its attachments.
This is how you find the id of a deleted channel, so you can recover those
attachments with recover-attachments and locate the channel in a data export.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### discorddol.tools.guilds(, token=None)

List the Discord servers the bot has been added to.

Run this first: if it returns an empty list, the bot exists but has not been invited
to any server yet.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### discorddol.tools.messages(guild, channel, , token=None, limit=None, include_threads=False)

Fetch a channel’s messages as dicts. `limit=None` fetches the whole history.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### discorddol.tools.post_message(channel_id, text, , token=None)

Post a message to a channel. Requires the bot to have Send Messages.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### discorddol.tools.recover_attachments(channel_id, , out_dir='~/Downloads/discord_recovered', cache_dir=None)

Write out every attachment this machine cached for a channel, deleted or not.

Needs no token and no network: the bytes come from the local Discord client cache.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### discorddol.tools.transcript(guild, channel, , token=None, limit=None, include_threads=True)

Render a channel as readable transcript text – the form to feed an LLM.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
